subject.title: [Bug]: Slack `allowBots: true` silently drops all bot messages unless `allowFrom` contains an explicit owner user ID

question: Should Slack preserve the explicit-owner presence guard for wildcard-only `allowBots` room configs and add diagnostics, or add an explicit opt-in mode that admits all bot-authored room messages?
rationale: The current behavior is a shipped security guard, but it silently breaks real Slack bot/app workflows under a plausible wildcard config; choosing diagnostics, a new unsafe mode, or wildcard semantics changes the Slack authorization boundary.

options.title: Warn and preserve guard
options.body: Add Slack config/doctor/startup diagnostics for ownerless `allowBots` room setups while keeping explicit owner IDs or channel `users` required for room bot messages.

options.title: Add explicit all-bot mode
options.body: Introduce a clearly named opt-in mode for trusted deployments that bypasses owner presence, with security docs and regression tests.

options.title: Treat wildcard as owner presence
options.body: Make wildcard `allowFrom` satisfy bot-room owner presence, restoring intuitive wildcard behavior but weakening the prior security fix for existing configs.

recommendation.title: Warn and preserve guard
recommendation.body: Add Slack config/doctor/startup diagnostics for ownerless `allowBots` room setups while keeping explicit owner IDs or channel `users` required for room bot messages.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the owner-presence guard and recently closed a related Slack bot-admission allowlist PR with maintainer guidance on the desired trust model.
